title: Acropolis of Athens
summary: The Acropolis is the rocky hill above Athens, fortified from the 13th century BCE and a sanctuary of Athena from the 8th. Pericles' building programme added the Parthenon, built 447-438 BCE. The Parthenon later served as a church and a mosque and was wrecked in 1687 when Venetian bombardment struck an Ottoman powder store.

uncertainty.note: Start is the first fortification wall of the 13th century BC (UNESCO), astronomical -1299 to -1200; the Parthenon in the model was built 447-438 BC (Greek Ministry of Culture), with sculpture to 432 BC (MIT Libraries). End is the present.

phases.description: Periklean Parthenon (Parthenon III) built 447-438 BC by Iktinos and Kallikrates under Pheidias, replacing an earlier marble temple (Parthenon II) destroyed by the Persians in 480 BC.
Sculptural decoration completed (the MIT Libraries record dates the work 447-432 BCE).
The temple 'remained unchanged until the fifth century AD'; the end year is the midpoint of that century.
Converted into a church dedicated first to Saint Sophia and later to the Panagia; under Turkish rule a mosque. The Venetians under Morosini besieged the Acropolis in 1687.

On 26 September 1687 the Venetians bombarded the Parthenon, then used as a munitions store, and largely destroyed it; Lord Elgin removed much sculpture in the early nineteenth century. Conservation took place in 1896-1900 and 1922-1933 and a restoration programme has run since 1975.

reviewer_note: Shape temple_colonnade for the Parthenon; the place record is the whole Acropolis (UNESCO: about 170 by 350 m, hill 156 m). Least sure of the building's full height: only column height (10.43 m, Acropolis Restoration Service) was sourced, not the roof ridge, so treat it as a minimum. The 'intact' end year is the midpoint of 'the fifth century AD'. The MIT length and width sit in the page's embedded metadata JSON, which spotcheck strips; confirmed by reading the raw page. Coordinates are the Parthenon way in OpenStreetMap, about 70 m from UNESCO's point for the property.
